whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Field Service Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Service Cloud consultants expanding scope
personas.description: You configure Field Service and want to show that you can design mobile workforce solutions.

personas.label: Field operations managers
personas.description: You coordinate dispatchers and technicians and need to understand scheduling and field operations.

personas.label: Implementation partners
personas.description: You implement Salesforce Field Service for customers and want to validate your solution skills.

examDifficulty.heading: How to Prepare for the Exam
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers the Field Service and Operations consultant role. The largest listed domains are Managing Scheduling and Optimization (28%) and Managing Work Orders (23%). Review every domain in the current guide.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
63% to pass, which is 38 correct answers out of 60.
Prerequisites: Hold both Platform Administrator and Agentforce Service Consultant credentials.
Topics to review: Work orders, resources, scheduling, mobile work, inventory, assets, maintenance, and access.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use practice questions to find topics to revisit, then check your understanding against the official outline and Salesforce Help. A practice score does not guarantee an exam result.

examFormat.heading: Exam Format and Study Approach
examFormat.intro: The exam guide lists 60 scored multiple-choice or multiple-select questions, up to five unscored questions, and 105 minutes. Fees are US$200 for registration and US$100 for a retake, plus applicable taxes.
bestWayToPass: Review every domain in the official exam outline, including scheduling, work orders, mobile, inventory, assets and sharing.
Trace a job from Work Order through Service Appointment to resource assignment and completion.
Separate resource eligibility from the scheduling objective or preference.
Use practice questions to find gaps, then verify product behavior in Salesforce Help.

certificationCard.description: This credential covers designing and deploying Field Service and Operations solutions. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 63% pass mark, weighted towards Managing Scheduling and Optimization (28%) and Managing Work Orders (23%).

keyConcepts.h2: Field Service Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Core records and relationships
blocks.body: A Work Order describes the work to be done. Work Order Line Items break that work into tasks. A Service Appointment represents the planned visit, and a Service Resource is the person, crew or equipment assigned to it. Assets identify customer equipment. Follow the links between the Case, Work Order, appointment and assigned resource.

blocks.heading: Scheduling and dispatch
blocks.body: Dispatchers use the Dispatcher Console and its Gantt view to review and assign appointments. A Scheduling Policy gives the scheduler rules and objectives. The scheduler can weigh requirements such as skills, territory, availability and travel. Manual assignment and automated optimization are different ways to schedule work.

blocks.heading: Territories, resources and skills
blocks.body: A Service Territory groups work by a geographic or logical area. Service Territory Members connect resources to territories for a period of time. Skills and required skill levels help determine whether a resource is qualified. Check these records along with availability when diagnosing an assignment.

blocks.heading: Mobile work
blocks.body: The Field Service mobile app lets technicians review assigned work and update records from a mobile device. Offline behavior depends on the configured mobile app and its data settings. Confirm which records and actions must be available without a connection.

blocks.heading: Parts and inventory
blocks.body: Product Required records describe parts planned for a Work Order. Product Consumed records track parts actually used. Compare planned and actual quantities when reconciling a job. Inventory locations and transfers support the movement of stock.

scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify the job, appointment, resource and scheduling constraint before choosing a setting.

blocks.heading: Start with the resource
blocks.body: Check territory membership, required skills and availability before considering a preferred worker.

blocks.heading: Follow the appointment lifecycle
blocks.body: Review the Service Appointment status and required fields before changing scheduling configuration.

blocks.heading: Compare planned and used parts
blocks.body: Product Required records describe expected parts; Product Consumed records capture what the technician used.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this consultant certification, you can add adjacent clouds or deepen your specialisation:

sampleQuestions.question: Which Field Service record represents a worker or other resource that can receive an assignment?
options: A booked customer visit
A geographic service area
A schedule of working times
Service Resource
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Resource is the best fit because a Service Resource represents a person or other resource used in field operations. Availability is affected by related configuration and is not simply a property of the record alone.
whyWrong: A booked customer visit is not the best choice because service Appointment represents scheduled work, not technician availability itself.
A geographic service area is not the best choice because service Territory defines a geographic/logical area, not individual technician availability.

A schedule of working times is not the best choice because operating Hours define when a resource/location is generally open, but Service Resource specifically represents the technician's availability record.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Field Service Scheduling Policy tell the optimizer?
options: Assign each worker to a territory
Track all scheduled customer visits
Scheduling Policy rules and objectives
Manage inventory for every service location
sampleQuestions.explanation: Scheduling Policy rules and objectives is the best fit because scheduling Policies define work rules (constraints) and objectives that the scheduling optimizer uses when assigning appointments.
whyWrong: Assign each worker to a territory is not the best choice because assigning resources to territories is a separate configuration, not what a Scheduling Policy defines.
Track all scheduled customer visits is not the best choice because tracking service appointments is a record-management function, not what a Scheduling Policy defines.
Manage inventory for every service location is not the best choice because managing parts inventory is a separate Field Service function, unrelated to Scheduling Policy's optimizer rules.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tool lets technicians review schedules and update work while offline?
options: Service Console for desktop agents
Field Service Mobile
Lightning Experience for office users
Dispatcher Console for dispatchers
sampleQuestions.explanation: Field Service Mobile is the best fit because the Field Service Mobile App allows technicians to access schedules, update work orders, and capture signatures even without internet connectivity.
whyWrong: Service Console for desktop agents is not the best choice because service Console is a general Salesforce interface, not the mobile offline-capable app for technicians.
Lightning Experience for office users is not the best choice because lightning Experience is the general desktop interface, not the mobile offline app for field technicians.
Dispatcher Console for dispatchers is not the best choice because dispatcher Console is used by dispatchers in the office, not by field technicians in the field.

sampleQuestions.question: Which details determine whether a technician qualifies for an appointment?
options: The technician’s Salesforce profile
Permission sets assigned to the technician
The technician’s place in the role hierarchy
Skills and territory membership
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skills and territory membership is the best fit because skill Requirements on the Work Type and Service Territory membership determine which Service Resources are eligible for scheduling.
whyWrong: The technician’s Salesforce profile is not the best choice because user Profile alone controls broad access, not the specific scheduling eligibility criteria.
Permission sets assigned to the technician is not the best choice because permission Sets grant feature access, not specifically scheduling eligibility.
The technician’s place in the role hierarchy is not the best choice because role Hierarchy determines record visibility, not specifically technician scheduling eligibility.

sampleQuestions.question: Where can a dispatcher see appointments plotted across a timeline?
options: A calendar list showing appointment dates
A record list sorted by appointment time
A territory map showing service locations
Dispatcher Console Gantt
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dispatcher Console Gantt is the best fit because the Dispatcher Console Gantt shows a visual timeline of scheduled appointments across service resources.
whyWrong: A calendar list showing appointment dates is not the best choice because calendar View shows a different, less operationally detailed schedule view.
A record list sorted by appointment time is not the best choice because list View shows tabular data, not the visual timeline dispatchers use.
A territory map showing service locations is not the best choice because map View shows geographic location, not the visual scheduling timeline being described.

sampleQuestions.question: What setup record provides default work-order details such as duration, skills and parts?
options: Track inventory without linking it to a job
Choose the service territory for every customer
Work Type
Build reports about completed jobs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Work Type is the best fit because work Type defines the template for work orders including duration and skill requirements.
whyWrong: Track inventory without linking it to a job is not the best choice because 'To track inventory only' misattributes Work Type's purpose to a different Field Service function.
Choose the service territory for every customer is not the best choice because assigning territories is a separate configuration, unrelated to Work Type's template purpose.
Build reports about completed jobs is not the best choice because creating reports is a separate function, unrelated to Work Type's template purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: How is a scheduled Service Appointment related to its Work Order?
options: A Service Resource assigned to the job
Service Appointment under its Work Order
Operating Hours linked to the territory
A Service Territory linked to the customer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Appointment under its Work Order is the best fit because service Appointments are child records of Work Orders.
whyWrong: A Service Resource assigned to the job is not the best choice because service Resource represents the technician, not the object linking appointment to work order.
Operating Hours linked to the territory is not the best choice because operating Hours define availability windows, not the appointment-to-work-order link.
A Service Territory linked to the customer is not the best choice because service Territory defines a geographic area, not the appointment-to-work-order link.

sampleQuestions.question: Which factors can the optimizer use when it assigns an appointment?
options: The territory by itself, without resource details
Skills, time, travel and policy
Skills alone, regardless of availability
Travel time alone, regardless of job requirements
sampleQuestions.explanation: Skills, time, travel and policy is the best fit because the optimizer considers skills, availability, travel, and policies.
whyWrong: The territory by itself, without resource details is not the best choice because 'Only territory' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of skills, travel time, and policies.
Skills alone, regardless of availability is not the best choice because 'Only skills' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of availability, travel time, and policies.
Travel time alone, regardless of job requirements is not the best choice because 'Only travel time' undersells the optimizer's broader consideration of skills, availability, and policies.

sampleQuestions.question: Which dispatcher view supports manual appointment drag-and-drop?
options: A list view used to edit records
Dispatcher Console Gantt
A map view used to locate service addresses
A report used to summarize appointment history
sampleQuestions.explanation: Dispatcher Console Gantt is the best fit because the Gantt allows manual drag-and-drop scheduling.
whyWrong: A list view used to edit records is not the best choice because list View alone doesn't support drag-and-drop scheduling, that's the Gantt's specific function.
A map view used to locate service addresses is not the best choice because map View alone doesn't support drag-and-drop scheduling, that's the Gantt's specific function.
A report used to summarize appointment history is not the best choice because reports display data, they don't support interactive drag-and-drop scheduling.

sampleQuestions.question: What availability windows can Operating Hours define?
options: Define skill requirements for each worker
Record which parts are in the van
Resource and location availability windows
Create work orders for new jobs
sampleQuestions.explanation: Resource and location availability windows is the best fit because operating Hours define availability windows for resources and locations.
whyWrong: Define skill requirements for each worker is not the best choice because 'To define skills only' undersells Operating Hours, which is about availability windows, not skills.
Record which parts are in the van is not the best choice because 'To track parts only' misattributes Operating Hours' purpose to a different Field Service function.
Create work orders for new jobs is not the best choice because 'To create work orders' misattributes Operating Hours' purpose to a different Field Service function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which records track parts planned for or used on work orders?
options: Service Resource records for each worker
Work Type records for common job templates
Product Required / Product Consumed
Service Territory records for dispatch areas
sampleQuestions.explanation: Product Required / Product Consumed is the best fit because product Required and Product Consumed track parts on work orders.
whyWrong: Service Resource records for each worker is not the best choice because service Resource represents the technician, not the parts-tracking object.
Work Type records for common job templates is not the best choice because work Type defines the job template, not the specific parts-tracking object.
Service Territory records for dispatch areas is not the best choice because service Territory defines a geographic area, unrelated to tracking parts.

sampleQuestions.question: Which tasks can technicians complete in the Field Service mobile app?
options: View the schedule only while online
Run reports but not update service records
Offline work, signatures and photos
View dashboards without appointment details
sampleQuestions.explanation: Offline work, signatures and photos is the best fit because the mobile app supports offline work, signatures, and photos.
whyWrong: View the schedule only while online is not the best choice because 'Online only' is the opposite of what the mobile app's offline capability provides.
Run reports but not update service records is not the best choice because 'Reports only' undersells the mobile app's broader field capabilities (offline, signatures, photos).
View dashboards without appointment details is not the best choice because 'Dashboards only' undersells the mobile app's broader field capabilities (offline, signatures, photos).

sampleQuestions.question: What enables the system to assign appointments automatically using optimization rules?
options: Manual assignment by a dispatcher only
The Gantt display with no scheduling service
A map that only shows service locations
Optimization with Scheduling Policies
sampleQuestions.explanation: Optimization with Scheduling Policies is the best fit because the optimization service runs with scheduling policies for automatic assignment.
whyWrong: Manual assignment by a dispatcher only is not the best choice because manual assignment is the opposite of the automated optimization being asked about.
The Gantt display with no scheduling service is not the best choice because gantt alone is a visualization tool, not the automated scheduling engine itself.
A map that only shows service locations is not the best choice because map View alone is a visualization tool, not the automated scheduling engine itself.

sampleQuestions.question: How does a Service Territory help organize field work?
options: Track parts without identifying a work area
Geographic or logical service areas
Create standard job templates for each customer
Record service contracts and billing terms
sampleQuestions.explanation: Geographic or logical service areas is the best fit because service Territories define areas for resource assignment and routing.
whyWrong: Track parts without identifying a work area is not the best choice because 'To track parts only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.
Create standard job templates for each customer is not the best choice because 'To create work types only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.
Record service contracts and billing terms is not the best choice because 'To manage contracts only' misattributes Service Territory's purpose to a different Field Service function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Field Service features represent covered services and service-level commitments?
options: Work Types to define expected job details
Operating Hours to set availability windows
Service Resources to list assigned workers
Service Contracts and Entitlements
sampleQuestions.explanation: Service Contracts and Entitlements is the best fit because service Contracts and Entitlements define SLAs and covered services.
whyWrong: Work Types to define expected job details is not the best choice because work Type alone defines job templates, not entitlement/SLA tracking.
Operating Hours to set availability windows is not the best choice because operating Hours alone define availability windows, not entitlement/SLA tracking.
Service Resources to list assigned workers is not the best choice because service Resource alone represents technicians, not entitlement/SLA tracking.

sampleQuestions.question: A dispatcher wants certain field technicians to see only the scheduled appointments assigned to their own crew, not every appointment in the org. What should the consultant configure?
options: Sharing rules or settings that scope Service Appointment visibility to the resource's crew
A new Work Type for each crew
A different Operating Hours record for each technician, with a separate Service Territory per crew
A Maintenance Plan per crew
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing Service Appointments appropriately, scoped to a resource's crew or territory, is exactly what the Permissions and Sharing domain covers.
whyWrong: A new Work Type defines job templates, it doesn't control who can see which appointments.
Operating Hours define availability windows, not record visibility.
A Maintenance Plan schedules preventive work, it doesn't control appointment sharing.

sampleQuestions.question: Equipment at a customer site needs preventive service visits generated automatically on a recurring schedule. What should the consultant set up?
options: A Maintenance Plan linked to the Asset
A one-off Work Order with no recurrence
A Service Territory
A Schedule Policy
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Maintenance Plan linked to an Asset generates Work Orders on a recurring schedule for preventive maintenance, exactly what's needed here.
whyWrong: A one-off Work Order doesn't recur automatically, it's a single job.
A Service Territory organizes field work geographically, it doesn't generate recurring visits.
A Schedule Policy guides the optimizer's scheduling rules, it doesn't create the recurring work itself.

sampleQuestions.question: A part is installed on a customer's equipment during a service visit. How should the consultant track which part now belongs to that equipment?
options: Update the Asset record and its relationship to the Product Consumed
Delete the old Asset record
Ignore it, parts aren't tracked after installation
Create a new Work Order for the visit with no reference to the installed part
sampleQuestions.explanation: Managing Assets includes updating Asset records and their relationships when parts are installed, so the system reflects what's actually on the customer's equipment.
whyWrong: Deleting the Asset record would lose the equipment's service history.
Parts used in service visits are specifically tracked through Products Consumed and Asset relationships.
A Work Order with no part reference wouldn't document what was installed.

sampleQuestions.question: A technician's van needs to carry the right parts for scheduled jobs, and the dispatcher wants to know what stock is on that van. What supports this?
options: A van as a Service Resource with an associated Product Inventory location
A Work Type
An Operating Hours record that lists the days the van is in use by each technician
A Schedule Policy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Modeling a van as a Service Resource (or linked location) with Product Inventory tracks what stock is available on that van, part of the Managing Inventory domain.
whyWrong: A Work Type defines job templates, not inventory locations.
Operating Hours define availability, not stock tracking.
A Schedule Policy guides the optimizer, it doesn't track van inventory.

sampleQuestions.question: A field service mobile user needs to capture a customer's signature confirming work is complete. What supports this?
options: Customer sign-off configured in the Field Service mobile app
A desktop-only report
Operating Hours
A Service Territory member record with the customer's name added to it
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer sign-off is a Field Service mobile app capability that lets a technician capture a signature confirming completed work, part of Configuring Mobility.
whyWrong: A desktop-only report doesn't work in the field where the technician needs to capture a signature on-site.
Operating Hours define availability, unrelated to signature capture.
A Service Territory member record defines territory assignment, not sign-off capture.
